newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK councillor defends post-1997 political changes.
newsitem.headline: HK councillor defends post-1997 political changes.

text.p: A member of Hong Kong's future executive council, Tam Yiu-chung, on Sunday defended a new set of proposed changes to civil liberties in Hong Kong after it reverts from British to Chinese rule on July 1.
Proposals to restrict public protests and foreign funding of political parties have met with strenuous opposition, but Tam said they were needed to protect Hong Kong after the handover.

"There are small groups of people who might be affected by foreign political influences and powers who have ulterior motives. In order to protect ourselves, we have to say these are the things you cannot do," Tam, speaking Chinese, told a public meeting on Sunday.
Following the panel, Tam told reporters that prevention of foreign political influences was the new government's goal.
"Sometimes on legal matters, preparation averts peril. It is not necessary that we wait until serious things happen to make laws. This is not a responsible way to act," Tam said.
Tung Chee-hwa, Hong Kong's future chief executive, has proposed a series of laws rolling back civil liberties in Hong Hong after the handover.
The proposals sparked outcry both overseas and in Hong Kong, which was promised considerable autonomy under the "one country, two systems" policy guiding the handover.
